name: Super Visuals Backgrounds
tagline: Private Figma design file of background visuals; needs a Figma login to open
description: A Figma working file named "Super Visuals — Backgrounds Library" holding a set of background and visual assets. The URL is a /design/ editor link, not a Figma Community publication, so it resolves to the Figma app shell and shows no public metadata (og:title is the generic "Figma", og:description "Created with Figma"). Contents, asset count, author and license could not be verified without an authenticated Figma session. Treat it as a personal or team file bookmark rather than a distributable resource.
agent_guidance: Do not reach for this in an automated workflow — a /design/ Figma URL is an editor link and returns only the app shell to any unauthenticated fetch, so you cannot read frames, export assets, or count what is inside. If a user asks for these specific backgrounds, ask them to duplicate the file to Figma Community or export the frames as PNG/SVG first. For programmatically reachable background assets, prefer Grainient or a Figma Community file instead.
why_it_matters: It is a reminder that a large share of saved design references are private Figma links that no agent and no future teammate can open. Value here is entirely gated behind one person's Figma account.
notable_for: private Figma editor link, not a Community file
evidence: GET https://www.figma.com/design/1RjQY50dy7t9SucZtAIb1p/Super-Visuals--Backgrounds-Library.?node-id=1-2&p=f (HTTP 200, 817KB app shell, og:title="Figma", og:description="Created with Figma"); WebFetch of the same URL returned only the word "Figma"; web search for "Super Visuals" backgrounds library found no matching public product

name: Grainient
tagline: 1,409 grainy, smooth and AI-rendered background assets in 4K to 12K
description: Grainient is a paid background-asset library by Basit A. Khan: 375 noisy/grainy gradients, 406 smooth blend gradients, 90 abstract animated gradients and 538 AI-generated backgrounds, packaged into 61 named collections. Downloads run 4K to 12K for stills and 2K–4K at 30–60fps for the animated loops, and a browser shader tool at shader.grainient.supply generates custom variations. Commercial rights are included with either plan, and a small Freebies section is open to everyone. It is aimed at designers and front-end devs who need a hero or landing-page background that does not look like every other mesh gradient.

name: Fontshare
tagline: 100 free font families, 926 styles, served from a public CSS API
description: Fontshare is the free font service from the Indian Type Foundry. It ships 100 families across 926 individual styles — 64 families under ITF's own free font licence (personal and commercial use) and 36 under SIL OFL — including widely used originals such as Satoshi, General Sans, Clash Display, Switzer, Cabinet Grotesk, Zodiak and Bespoke Sans. Every family is downloadable as desktop and web files, 82 families ship at least one variable style, and a Google-Fonts-style CSS endpoint at api.fontshare.com serves woff2/woff straight from cdn.fontshare.com. It is the default alternative to Google Fonts when you want something with more personality than Inter.
pricing_detail: Free. No account required for download or CDN use.
agent_guidance: Use this instead of Google Fonts when the brief says "not another Inter site" — Satoshi, General Sans, Switzer and Clash Display are the workhorses, and Zodiak/Bespoke Serif cover the editorial serif case. Wire it up with the CSS endpoint (`https://api.fontshare.com/v2/css?f[]=<slug>@400,500,700&display=swap`) rather than committing font files, and query `https://api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts?limit=100` if you need to pick a family programmatically — that JSON is unauthenticated and returns the whole catalogue with weights, categories, designers and OpenType features. Watch the licence split: 36 families are SIL OFL, but 64 are under ITF's own free font licence, so check `license_type` before redistributing or embedding the files in a product you resell. The website itself is a JS-only shell — hit the API, not the HTML.
why_it_matters: The single best source of genuinely free, professionally drawn display and text faces on the web, and the only one of its size with a clean public API an agent can query directly.
notable_for: home of Satoshi, General Sans, Clash Display
evidence: https://fontshare.com (HTTP 200 but JS-only shell), https://api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts?limit=100&offset=0 (HTTP 200, count_total=100, full catalogue paginated to exhaustion — 926 styles, license_type split itf_ffl 64 / sil_ofl 36, 82 families with a variable style), https://api.fontshare.com/v2/css?f[]=general-sans@400,500&display=swap (HTTP 200, returns @font-face rules pointing at cdn.fontshare.com)

name: Craftwork Curated
tagline: 2,212 curated websites plus 2,230 UI sections, filed under 15 industries
description: Craftwork Curated is the inspiration arm of Craftwork, the Bangkok-based design marketplace; it absorbed the old Curated.design gallery. The /curated/websites index holds 2,212 full-site captures filed under 15 industry categories, and a parallel /curated/section index holds 2,230 individual page sections for when you need one hero or one pricing block rather than a whole site. Browsing is free; the wider Craftwork marketplace (3,000+ packs, 40,000+ assets) sits behind Pro Access, which also unlocks a Figma plugin and an MCP server that lets an agent semantic-search the asset library.
pricing_detail: Curated browsing is free. Pro Access: $49/mo individual, $69/mo team; $199/yr individual ($17/mo), $299/yr team ($25/mo); $324 one-time lifetime (individual only). Monthly caps at 10 pack downloads, 300 individual assets and 500 MCP requests per month; yearly and lifetime are unlimited downloads with 5,000 MCP requests/month. All tiers include the Figma plugin, commercial licence, unlimited Curated Inspiration, and you keep files after cancelling.
agent_guidance: Use this when you need visual precedent before writing layout code — the 15 industry filters (agency, artificial-intelligence, assets, design-tools, desktop-apps, development-tools, finance, marketing, mobile-apps, portfolio, productivity, shops, tech, web-apps, web3) let you pull a tight reference set for the client's vertical, and /curated/section is the better entry point when you only need one block. The HTML is client-rendered and useless to fetch, so enumerate entries from https://craftwork.design/server-sitemap-curated.xml and then fetch individual /curated/website/<slug> pages. If the user already pays for Pro, the Craftwork MCP server (set up via the @craftwork-design/wizard npm wizard, OAuth after install) is the only agent-native path into the 40,000-asset library — but it is Pro-gated and rate-limited to 500 or 5,000 requests a month, so do not build a pipeline that hammers it.
why_it_matters: One of the very few inspiration galleries at this scale that also publishes a full sitemap and an MCP server, which makes it usable by an agent rather than only by a human scrolling screenshots.
evidence: https://craftwork.design/curated/websites (HTTP 200, JS-rendered; category icon paths reveal the 15 categories), https://craftwork.design/mcp (MCP server, @craftwork-design/wizard, Pro-gated, OAuth), https://craftwork.design/pro (full pricing table), https://craftwork.design/sitemap.xml and https://craftwork.design/server-sitemap-curated.xml (4,458 locs: 2,212 /curated/website, 2,230 /curated/section, 16 /curated/websites category pages). /api/curated and /llms.txt both 404.

name: BentoGrids
tagline: 285 real bento-grid layouts captured from shipping sites and brand work
description: BentoGrids, by Ivan Volti, is a single-pattern gallery: 285 screenshots and clips of bento-style grids, split into 203 UI examples (Apple, Vercel Geist, Frame.io, Mintlify, Medusa, Nuxt Labs, Tailwind UI, Neon, Dovetail, Gitbook) and 82 graphic/branding treatments. Each entry links back to its source site, so you can see the pattern in production rather than as a mockup. It also gives away free Figma bento grid templates. Free, no account needed to browse.

templates.name: Bento Grid Template #1
templates.purpose: Free Figma bento grid layout with alternative grid variations

templates.name: Bento Grid Template #2
templates.purpose: Second free Figma bento grid layout

pricing_detail: Free to browse. Free Figma templates delivered by email sign-up at /templates.
agent_guidance: Pull this up before you build a feature or product-overview section as a bento grid — 285 shipped examples will tell you how big the hero cell should be and how the pattern degrades on mobile, which is where most hand-rolled bento layouts fall apart. Unusually for a gallery, the homepage is server-rendered: fetch https://bentogrids.com with a normal browser user-agent and parse `__NEXT_DATA__` for the full `shots` array (id, title, category `ui`/`graphic`, sourceLink, asset dimensions) — WebFetch alone returns an empty shell. It gives you references and Figma files, never code, so pair it with a Tailwind grid or shadcn/ui cards for the actual implementation.
why_it_matters: The definitive index for one very overused pattern — having 285 real examples in one place is what stops a bento grid from turning into a generic feature card wall.

name: H1 Gallery
tagline: 220 numbered product headlines from real landing pages, updated weekly
description: H1 Gallery is an archive of marketing headlines — the literal H1 of a product's landing page — collected and numbered H-001 through H-220, each credited to the product it came from (Vercel, Cursor, Lovable, Linktree, Perplexity Comet, Granola, Webflow, Evernote, incident.io and a long tail of indie SaaS). It is curated by Corey Haines, cofounder of the SaaS marketing agency Conversion Factory, with a free Friday newsletter that breaks down three headlines a week with commentary from the founders behind them. Free, no paywall, and the whole archive renders server-side on one page.
pricing_detail: Free. Weekly email newsletter, free to subscribe.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when you are writing hero copy, not designing a hero — it is the fastest way to calibrate headline length, specificity and voice against 220 shipped examples before you draft. The entire archive is in the server-rendered HTML of the homepage, so a single fetch of https://h1gallery.com gives you every headline paired with its product name; you can grep it for a vertical ("Mac", "AI agent", "analytics") to build a tight reference set. Do not copy a headline verbatim into a client's site — use it to fix the pattern (concrete promise, specific noun, no adjective stacking), and pair it with an actual layout source like Craftwork Curated for the visual half.
why_it_matters: Copy is the part of a landing page an AI agent most often gets generic, and this is one of the only curated corpora of headlines that actually shipped rather than headline advice in the abstract.
notable_for: each credited to a real product
evidence: https://h1gallery.com (HTTP 200, 1.2MB, full archive H-220 down to H-001 read from server-rendered HTML), https://h1gallery.com/about (HTTP 200, curator Corey Haines / Conversion Factory, weekly Friday newsletter, @H1gallery on X, © 2025)
